text: Signal doesn't need to travel too far away. This means that we can cope with higher frequencies. If instead we want to connect the transmitter and receiver that are very far away from each other, then using high frequencies is not a good idea because the signal gets attenuated very much, and therefore we need to have a two-way signal at the receiver. Okay, so as often in life, it's a matter of trading off advantages with disadvantages. Consider however that the current trend in wireless communications is to use higher frequencies and to have transmitters and receivers closer to each other. That's the trend in all technologies: WiFi, cellular. So we say that wireless networks get denser and denser. It's the so-called densification phenomenon of wireless networks. To have nodes that communicate with each other, we closer and closer and be able to use higher frequencies. The advantage of that is, as mentioned, that in this case we are able to first of all use a portion of the spectrum at high frequencies, where there are more radio resources. So there is more, let's see, space to transmit signals in.
